label: early original-phase u/s/t/p input after e/z/j/c/b-type context
explanation: Sparse update-gate unit. About 95% of its activation mass falls in the original phase at steps 2-4, and 71% at step 3 alone. It is never active at steps 0-1, at the delimiter, or past step 5, apart from a small copy-phase tail at recall_idx 1 (about 5% of mass, mostly L=3, where the fed-back orig(0) is u/s/t/x). The input token is mostly u (40% of mass) or s (30%), with t and p next. It is mostly a first occurrence of that token. Whether it fires also depends on the earlier tokens: e, z, j, c, b, w, v or 0 at positions 0-2 raise the rate (strongest when first_tok is e), and the largest activations look like e ? ? u. The token-and-position condition alone covers 85% of the mass but has only 7% precision. Requiring two or more of those context tokens raises dev F1 to 0.34 (mass recall 0.62). The rule behind the context dependence looks like a distributed function of the hidden state, which no simple token-set predicate captures.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=u (+6.69), in_tok=s (+6.25), in_tok=t (+4.48), in_tok=p (+4.00), prev_tok=c (+3.29), prev_tok=b (+3.10). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.58), prev2_tok=r (-3.52), prev_tok=r (-3.27), orig1=p (-3.17).
